content:
The Mathlib repository has an intimidating number of PRs. Many of these PRs have not been touched by the author for over a year and over half of them have not had any activity for over a month. Also, the contributing guide says, "Reviews of PRs, especially from new reviewers, are essentially always welcome." It would be helpful to these new reviewers (and I suspect old reviewers) to have a smaller set of PRs to filter over. What do you think of adding an auto-close stale PRs Github action? After all, closing a PR isn't all that destructive, the author could pretty easily reopen it.
Maybe the policy should be auto-close PRs if no activity for a month.
The recommended approach for people who want to review PRs is to use the #queueboard, which excludes most of the PR you mention. So I don't think it's that much of a problem.

Mathlib reviewers essentially never look at the full list of PRs as it appears on GitHub. Rather, they start at https://leanprover-community.github.io/queueboard/review_dashboard.html and use the filters available there to show PRs that are relevant to them. This is usually a manageable amount.
Oh, nice! Although, although that 3.1k next to "Pull requests" makes me uncomfortable. I'll get used to it.
I think @Nathanael Thompson 's point still stands though --- should there be an expiry date for PRs with no activity? Maybe not a month but a year?

This has been touched on in the past --- one counterpoint is that some PRs are of the "it would be worthwhile to have this, but needs somebody to adopt this work" category, and we have been reluctant to have a blanket policy. At the same time, this seems like a useful topic to discuss. I'll add it to the backlog of the maintainers agenda (at normal priority - so, probably this will be discussed, but could take a while).
Wouldn't that particular counterpoint be countered by a "Close after X time unless flagged with the Please adopt label" rule?
And potentially "discussion whether to add please adopt for each case" or "close after X time if please adopt has been up after Y time".
webpage#897 clarifies the contribution guide, to link the review queue

Michael Rothgang said:

"it would be worthwhile to have this, but needs somebody to adopt this work" category

In view of this, one problem with closing abandoned PRs is that it's not easy to filter those PRs among the ones that were closed due to being merged . Bors adds "merged by bors" in the title but you cannot filter against it. I think it could help to add a merged-by-bors label as GitHub can filter labels by exclusion
Oh, there is a bors-staging label. But I don't know enough about Bors to know if it always implies that the closed PR was actually merged
You can also just filter PRs with is:pr is:closed in:title NOT "Merged by Bors", yes?
Thanks, I didn't know about that (and I think it's not even documented in this "advanced search syntax" page?)

Nathanael Thompson said:

Maybe the policy should be auto-close PRs if no activity for a month.

I made 7 small PR's in RepresentationTheory and my feeling is that this subarea has very few active contributors/reviewers (to see this, just filter RepresentationTheory). Only the super easy two +4 lines are merged, while the others remain silent for a month. I would be happy to be explicitly told that my PR's are closed because they do not meet the quality standard, rather than being auto-closed because nobody reviews them in a month while I am still willing to maintain it.
One should obviously not count the time a PR is ready for review

If PRs were autoclosed after a few months of awaiting-author, the GitHub PR list would probably still be over 1000. I don't see how that would be an improvement over the current situation, given we have the queueboard already.

My 2 cents as an experienced software engineer:

  • "We keep the old PRs in case they will be helpful in the future"
    Generally it's less costly to just develop from scratch again than to adopt it to a future mainline, given that there will be new machinery available in the meantime etc.

  • "The PR is open for a long time because no one reviews"
    Any filtering should be based on "last activity" and not "PR creation" time. A PR staying open for a long time without activity likely has merge conflict or does not meet new standard etc. Open PR should be periodically bumped since there is little value in reviewing a stale PR with merge conflicts and/or not passing CI.

  • "Filtering by a single rule will only trim the PR queue from 3k to 2k"
    Incremental improvement is always better than nothing. There will unlikely be one rule that keeps the queue doable and clean so if we wait for one perfect rule nothing will ever be done.

  • "We have a board elsewhere that is managable"
    The purpose of Github PR tab is to have a board that is functioning. Having a dup increases friction and mental load. People wanting to review PRs need to come to Zulip and learn about the board. People on Zulip need to answer the question of "how does 3k PR queue work" once in a while.

  • "Need to link issue, PR and commits"
    Commit message should be the source of truth that links issue, PR and code change.

Might be interesting to look at pi which is another popular open source project at the other end of the spectrum: they auto close all PRs and maintainers manually reopen those ready for review.

@Anna Immerwahr what benefit is there from reducing open PRs with the current infrastructure we have? I really don't see one and in this thread none has been mentioned so far.
I could see a benefit from having <100 open PRs but this is not achievable. Reducing as you said from 3k to 2k in my eyes is not "incremental" but just no difference at all.

Personally, I have some open PRs that have had merge-conflict / awaiting-author for a long time, but would want to work on them eventually. It would make me quite uncomfortable to have a "deadline" (even if one could reopen PRs)

Anna Immerwahr said:

Generally it's less costly to just develop from scratch again than to adopt it to a future mainline,

A PR staying open for a long time without activity likely has merge conflict or does not meet new standard etc.

There is a bot to add a tag for merge conflicts (which you can then filter out in the PR tab if you like.) Otherwise, I don't think these points are true for mathlib, and I'm not sure they're true for general software engineering either.

People wanting to review PRs need to come to Zulip and learn about the board.

The likelihood someone knows enough about Lean and mathlib to contribute reviews without having spent a fair amount of time on this Zulip or clicking around on the mathlib site is basically zero.

Thanks for your input; since I'm not a software engineer by training, such a perspective is valuable.

Let me I disagree with

The purpose of Github PR tab is to have a board that is functioning.

If only github were to offer "a board that is functioning"! The queueboard was created precisely because of shortcomings in its model (including no proper reporting of the last meaningful update, as opposed to "a bot walks across your PR"). It is unfortunate to have this duplication, but I don't think "use github" is an easy (nor managable) fix.

Since this discussion is generating a lot of comments, I'll pitch in with my somewhat tongue in cheek two scents. As another veteran software engineer, I tend to agree with Anna Immerwahr . Maybe the inclination is due to having to deal with a billion different standards for everything (https://xkcd.com/927/) because every group thinks that the standards of another group is insufficient. Meanwhile, everybody has to deal with a different queueboard for each open source project they contribute to. That said, I don't think its a big deal either way. Reopening a PR isn't hard, Just press the button.

One practise I've been trying out when reviewing (this isn't any official guideline, just me) on stale PRs with the awaiting-author label where I've reviewed before: Ping the author after 4 and 10 weeks of inactivity, then depending on the PRs content I would mark it as "draft" with either please-adopt or help-wanted, or close the PR with closed-due-to-inactivity (maybe will-close-soon first). Having done this for a while now, I believe it would not be desirable to do this completely automated. There are certainly stale PRs with high-value content where it would be sad to see them auto-closed. Recreating the PRs for such high-value contributions is probably more work than starting from the stale draft.

A few smaller suggestions:

  • the "draft" feature could be used more: PRs with WIP or please-adopt could IMO all be marked as drafts automatically. (note, this does not decrease the "3.1k" counter though, but it makes filtering easier and the displayed UI a bit more obvious)
  • have some automation to auto-close PRs once they have the will-close-soon label, together with some guidelines about how to use it as well as tooling for the author to counter-act (e.g. mark the PR as "draft" / "WIP" instead if they plan to come back to it in the future).

Anecdotally, I have the impression it's becoming increasingly common for new users to make a PR and then ignore any review comments on it, as if they expect their PR's to be merged on a take-it-or-leave-it basis; and this leads to a lot of PR's being left forever on "awaiting-author".

Perhaps we can have a policy that any user who has more than X PR's in the "awaiting-author" state (where X = 3 or 5 maybe) is not allowed to make any new PR's (and if they attempt to, their PR's get automatically closed)?
